scope: Online rooms, online player-versus-player fights, local two-player fights, and interruption/input edge cases.

environment.sessions: Separate default and incognito browser profiles
inputMethods: Synthetic touch PointerEvents in the real controls

build.note: Vite reports the existing large-bundle warning.

browserRegression.run: Evaluate the file as JavaScript in a browser tab with an active online fight.
browserRegression.beforeFix: A hidden online tab restored its held controller guard.
browserRegression.ci: Runs against the real Game component in the browser; it is separate from the Node test suite.

fixes.issue: Simultaneous final-stock knockouts or ringouts incorrectly awarded player 2 the win; some simultaneous losses were not counted.
fixes.cause: Stock loss selected a winner and returned before processing the other player.
fixes.change: Resolve both stock losses before selecting the winner; simultaneous final losses draw.
fixes.regression: tests/engine.test.ts: simultaneous final-stock knockouts and ringouts; simultaneous stock losses; tests/rooms.test.ts: online double knockouts

fixes.issue: A projectile knockout on the last clock tick could finish without deducting the lost stock.
fixes.cause: Stock loss ran before projectile collisions, then timeout ended the match.
fixes.change: Resolve projectile collisions before stock losses and timeout scoring.
fixes.regression: tests/engine.test.ts: projectile knockouts resolve before timeout, including simultaneous final hits

fixes.issue: A connection stall left movement, blocking, or platform-down held indefinitely.
fixes.cause: The server retained the last input until another input arrived or the socket disconnected.
fixes.change: Expire held controls after 500 ms without valid input while preserving action counters.
fixes.regression: tests/rooms.test.ts: stalled online input releases held controls without replaying actions, then recovers
fixes.browser: Dropping input updates for 850 ms now releases the guard; fresh input resumes control.

fixes.issue: A decreasing action counter could replay an action, including a second jump.
fixes.cause: The server accepted decreasing counters and the engine treated any counter change as a press.
fixes.change: Reject input frames containing a counter older than the last accepted frame.
fixes.regression: tests/rooms.test.ts: older action counters cannot trigger a second jump or overwrite held controls

fixes.issue: Input from a completed fight could enter a rematch and interfere with its first fresh action.
fixes.cause: Input messages had no match identity.
fixes.change: Include the current match ID in browser input messages and reject missing or mismatched IDs on the server.
fixes.regression: tests/rooms.test.ts: rematches reject previous-match input and accept the first fresh action
fixes.compatibility: The input protocol now requires matchId. Reload existing browser clients when deploying client and server together.

fixes.issue: Disconnecting player 1's controller reassigned player 2's controller to player 1.
fixes.cause: Each poll assigned logical players by compacting the currently connected controller list.
fixes.change: Preserve controller-to-player assignments, release disconnected controls, and assign replacement controllers to vacant players.
fixes.regression: tests/controls.test.ts: disconnecting P1's controller preserves P2's controls and assigns replacements to P1
fixes.browser: Reproduced [P1 light, P2 light] counters changing to [1,0] before the fix; after the fix they change to [0,1]. A replacement controller jumps as P1.

fixes.issue: A hidden online tab reasserted held controller inputs immediately after visibility cleanup.
fixes.cause: The animation loop polled gamepads while document.hidden was true.
fixes.change: Use the existing quiet-state gate, including hidden tabs, before polling gamepads.

interactiveChecks: Create a public room and join it through the public-room list.
Create a private room and join through a lowercase invitation URL.
Synchronize the guest's fighter choice to the host.
Disable stage selection for the guest.
Synchronize a host stage change and reset readiness.
Start the same match on both clients after both mark ready.
Skip presentations from either client while keeping the shared countdown.
Use player-1 keyboard controls for the guest's online fighter.
Connect light and heavy attacks from opposite sides.
Allow a double jump and reject a third jump.
Release online keyboard guard on blur.
Open the online pause menu while the server simulation continues.
Complete online fights and compare both clients' final results.
Wait for both rematch requests, reset health/lives, and carry forward the winner's unlock.
Disconnect the host during a fight, return the survivor to a waiting room, and transfer hosting.
Reconnect the disconnected client without retaining the old fight.
Move both local players simultaneously with separate keyboard mappings.
Use P2's number-row heavy attack against P1's guard without health loss.
Use P2's numeric-keypad heavy attack and observe P1 losing health.
Pause a local fight and verify the tick stops advancing.
Blur a local fight and verify both players release controls and the fight pauses.
Jump independently with two simulated controllers.
Disconnect P1's controller while preserving P2 ownership.
Connect a replacement controller and verify it belongs to P1.
Drop outgoing online input updates, verify held inputs expire, then resume control.
Hide an online tab with a controller guard held; verify only neutral input is sent until the tab resumes.
Use simultaneous touch movement and blocking as the online guest, release one finger independently, and jump.
Rotate the emulated mobile client to portrait; show the orientation gate and send neutral held controls without horizontal overflow.
Complete a production-build fight with 150 exactly equal same-tick snapshots and an identical final result.
Rematch on the production build and verify the first jump is accepted.
automatedCoverage: New regression tests cover both elimination orders, simultaneous health knockouts and ringouts, final-tick projectile deaths, online draws, input expiry/recovery, old counters, old-match inputs, and controller hotplug ownership.
A new real-WebSocket test checks synchronized movement and a special attack on all nine stages.
The existing suite covers the 41 fighters, room capacity, private invitations, malformed and oversized frames, simultaneous rooms, input isolation, rematches, and disconnects.
limits: Browser sessions and servers ran on the same machine. Actual WAN latency and packet loss were not measured; outgoing input delivery was deliberately interrupted for stall testing.
Gamepads and phone touch/orientation were simulated through browser APIs. Physical controllers, mobile Safari, and real phones were not available.
